I farm only 3 mu, but I have been doing this for 40 years, and I have well irrigation, so I will manage the land intensively rather than conservatively. Because my household has some off-farm work, I will keep the plan practical and stable instead of making it too labor-heavy. I grow wheat-maize in rotation, so I will use the full 3 mu for winter wheat first and then the same 3 mu for summer maize. For wheat, I will use improved seed, steady fertilizer, and enough irrigation to protect yield, because wheat in my area responds well to water and nitrogen when managed carefully. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is the most reliable way for me to keep yield high on a small irrigated farm. I will not overdo inputs, but I will not farm too lightly either, because with my experience and education I would rather aim for stable, above-average output than save a small amount on inputs and lose yield. I will use rotary tillage to keep field work efficient, control weeds and residues in a manageable way, and fit the short turnaround between wheat harvest and maize planting.
